complexity_factors: Multiple nested FORK_JOIN structures (2 levels deep)
4 DYNAMIC_FORK tasks requiring child workflow execution
Nested SWITCH containing FORK_JOIN with 3 parallel DYNAMIC_FORKs
Complex data transformations using JQ and inline JavaScript
LLM integration requiring external API calls
Multiple sub-workflow calls (5 total: security_get_device_id, vision_one_deep_visibility_hunt, vision_one_device_scan x2, Notify-Channels-x-mocked)
Deep data dependencies across multiple task layers

recommended_patterns.human_interaction: No human interaction patterns detected. Workflow is fully automated.
recommended_patterns.error_handling: RetryPolicy recommended for: llm_alert_analysis (OpenAI API calls), all DYNAMIC_FORK child workflows (external service calls)
recommended_patterns.parallel_execution: asyncio.gather recommended for: main FORK_JOIN (2 branches), nested FORK_JOIN (3 branches), 4 DYNAMIC_FORK tasks
recommended_patterns.loop_handling: No loops detected - continue-as-new not required
special_considerations: LLM_TEXT_COMPLETE task requires OpenAI SDK integration - implement as activity with retry policy
JSON_JQ_TRANSFORM tasks should be implemented as Python activities using pyjq library or native list comprehensions
INLINE JavaScript tasks should be translated to Python code - time functions use datetime module
Child workflows (security_get_device_id, vision_one_deep_visibility_hunt, vision_one_device_scan, Notify-Channels-x-mocked) must be implemented separately
DYNAMIC_FORK parallelism may be high - consider adding concurrency limits using semaphores if device/SHA256 lists are large
Deep nesting (2 levels) requires careful activity naming and result tracking - consider helper methods for nested branches
Mock data generation can be handled in workflow code or as separate activity depending on complexity preference
HTML email generation should use Python string formatting or Jinja2 templates
Workflow depends on OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable

translation_notes: This workflow demonstrates complex enterprise security orchestration with LLM-assisted threat analysis
The workflow has NO human interaction points - it is fully automated from start to finish

4 child workflows are referenced but not defined in this JSON - they must be migrated separately: security_get_device_id, vision_one_deep_visibility_hunt, vision_one_device_scan, Notify-Channels-x-mocked
LLM_TEXT_COMPLETE is a custom Conductor task type - implement as OpenAI API activity with proper prompt engineering
JSON_JQ_TRANSFORM tasks use JQ query language - can be implemented with pyjq library or translated to Python list comprehensions
INLINE tasks use GraalJS JavaScript - translate to equivalent Python code
The nested SWITCH->FORK_JOIN->DYNAMIC_FORK pattern is the most complex structure - use helper methods for clarity
Mock data contains realistic security alert examples for testing - preserve this data in test fixtures
All JOIN tasks are implicit in Temporal's asyncio.gather() pattern - no explicit join activities needed
Consider adding workflow queries to check scan progress and status
The workflow produces 2 outputs: notified_channel and action_recommendation - ensure these are returned in workflow output dataclass
